transcript.en: Thanks to all of you for coming along today to hear about how the robotic float project is helping with ocean research.
transcript.zh: 感谢各位的光临，今天主要讲解自动漂浮项目是如何有助于海洋研究的。

transcript.en: Well, first of all we'll look at what a robotic float does and its use.
transcript.zh: 首先，我们将看看什么是自动漂浮和如何使用。

transcript.en: So let's start with the device itself.
transcript.zh: 所以，让我们先从设备本身开始。

transcript.en: It looks a bit like a cigar and it's about one and a half metres long.
transcript.zh: 它看起来有点像雪茄，大约有一米半长。

transcript.en: More importantly it's full of equipment that's designed to collect data.
transcript.zh: 更重要的是，它装满了用来收集数据的装备。

transcript.en: So it can help us in building up a profile of different factors which work together within the world's oceans.
transcript.zh: 所以它为了我们研究世界大洋而建立起一个大洋的多面体。

transcript.en: Sounds like a big project - isn't it too big for one country to undertake?
transcript.zh: 听起来像是一个大工程，由一个国家来完成的话是不是量太大了？

transcript.en: That's quite true but this project is a really good example of international co-operation.
transcript.zh: 没错，不过这个项目是国际合作的好例子。

transcript.en: Over the last five years scientists from thirteen countries have been taking part in the project and launching floats in their area of ocean control.
transcript.zh: 在过去的5年里，来自13个国家的科学家参与到这个项目中，并且将漂浮物发射到他们各自海洋掌控的地方。

transcript.en: And next year this number will rise to fourteen when Indonesia joins the project.
transcript.zh: 明年当印尼加入到项目中时，参与国就是14个了。

transcript.en: That's impressive.
transcript.zh: 听上去不错。

transcript.en: But let's move onto how floats work.
transcript.zh: 但是让我们回到漂浮物的工作原理上。

transcript.en: The operational cycle goes like this.
transcript.zh: 运作周期是这样的。

transcript.en: Each of the floats is dropped in the ocean from a boat at a set point and activated from a satellite.
transcript.zh: 每一个漂浮物都是在设定点从船上放入海里，并且由卫星激活。

transcript.en: Then the float immediately sinks about 2,000 metres, that's two whole kilometres down in the water.
transcript.zh: 然后，漂浮物立即下沉到约2000米的位置，那是水下两公里。

transcript.en: It stays at this depth for about 10 days and is carried around by the currents which operate in the ocean at this level .
transcript.zh: 它位于这个深度停留十天左右，随波逐流，在海洋的这个水位上开展工作。

transcript.en: During this time it's possible for it to cover quite large distances but the average is fifty kilometres.
transcript.zh: 它在这段时期的覆盖距离可能非常大，但是平均是50公里。

transcript.en: So what is it actually recording?
transcript.zh: 那么它到底在记录什么？

transcript.en: Well at this stage nothing, but as it rises to the surface it collects all sorts of data most importantly variations in salinity,
transcript.zh: 在这个阶段什么也不记录。但是当它升到水面时就会记录各种数据。最重要的是盐度变化、

transcript.en: that's salt levels, and the changes in temperature, a bit like underwater weather balloons.
transcript.zh: 含盐量和温度变化，有点像水下的气象气球。

transcript.en: Then when it gets back to the surface all the data it's collected is beamed up to the satellite.
transcript.zh: 之后，当它到达水面时，所有收集的数据都会发向卫星。

transcript.en: After about five hours on the surface the float automatically sinks, beginning the whole process again.
transcript.zh: 漂浮物在水面停留大约5小时后会自动下沉，整个过程再次开始。

transcript.en: What happens to the data?
transcript.zh: 怎么处理那些数据？

transcript.en: Well the information is transferred direct to onshore meteorological stations... like our one in Hobart...
transcript.zh: 信息直接传送到海岸气象站，就像我们在霍巴特的气象站。

transcript.en: and within four hours the findings can be on computers and they can be mapped and analysed.
transcript.zh: 4小时内，结论就能出现在电脑上，并进行定位和分析。

transcript.en: You say you're building models of the world's ocean systems but how're they going to be used and more importantly, when?
transcript.zh: 你说过你们在建立世界海洋系统的模型，但是它们是如何使用的，更重要的是在什么时候用？

transcript.en: Some of the data has already helped in completing projects.
transcript.zh: 一些数据已经用于帮助完成项目。

transcript.en: For example our understanding of the underlying causes of El Niňo events is being confirmed by float data.
transcript.zh: 比如，我们对厄尔尼诺现象内在原因的理解可以由漂浮物搜集到的信息来确认。

transcript.en: Another way we're using float data is to help us to understand the mechanics of climate change like global warming and ozone depletion.
transcript.zh: 另外，我们利用漂浮体数据帮助我们了解气候变化的运行方式，比如全球变暖和臭氧层空洞。

transcript.en: That's part of an ongoing variability study but the results are still a long way off.
transcript.zh: 这只是持续存在的可变性研究的一部分，但是离结果还很远。

transcript.en: However, this is not the case with our ocean weather forecasting.
transcript.zh: 但是，这与我们的海洋天气预报的情况不同。

transcript.en: Because we know from the floats what the prevailing weather conditions will be in certain parts of the ocean, we can advise the navy on search and rescue missions.
transcript.zh: 因为我们从漂浮物可以得知海洋某一地区的主要天气条件，我们可以在搜查、营救任务中向海军提出建议。

transcript.en: That's happening right now and many yachtsmen owe their lives to the success of this project.
transcript.zh: 现在就是这样做的，而且许多游艇驾驶者因为这个项目的成功而获救。

transcript.en: In addition the float data can help us to look at the biological implications of ocean processes.
transcript.zh: 另外，漂浮体数据可以帮我们了解海洋的生物学意义。

transcript.en: Would that help with preserving fish stocks?
transcript.zh: 它能利于保护鱼类吗？

transcript.en: Yes, and advising governments on fisheries legislation.
transcript.zh: 是的，并且建议政府对渔业立法。

transcript.en: We're well on the way to completing a project on this.
transcript.zh: 我们正在完成这个项目。

transcript.en: We hope it will help to bring about more sustainable fishing practices.
transcript.zh: 我们希望这能有助于产生更多适当的捕鱼行为。

transcript.en: We'll be seeing the results of that quite soon.
transcript.zh: 我们很快会看到结果。

transcript.en: It sounds like the data from floats has lots of applications.
transcript.zh: 听起来漂浮体数据的用途很广。

transcript.en: Yes it does. It's also a powerful agricultural tool.
transcript.zh: 是的，它还是强大的农业工具。

transcript.en: If we were aware of what the weather would be like, say, next year,
transcript.zh: 假设我们能提前知道明年的天气情况，

transcript.en: we could make sure that the farmers planted appropriate grain varieties to produce the best yield from the available rainfall.
transcript.zh: 我们就指导农民种植一些合适的农作物产品，以确保在可用的雨水下获得最好的产量。

transcript.en: That sounds a bit like science fiction, especially when now we can't even tell them when a drought will break.
transcript.zh: 这听起来有点像科幻小说，特别是目前我们还无法告诉他们干旱何时会停止。

transcript.en: I agree that this concept is still a long way in the future, but it will come eventually and the float data will have made a contribution.
transcript.zh: 我同意这个概念在未来仍需很长一段时间去研究，但是它终究会实现，而且漂浮体数据也会为此出一份力。
